messages:
Maya: Drafted a lightweight EU-central-2 cluster bootstrap runbook and dropped the checklist. Can folks scan for missing validation steps? :wave:
Owen: Will review. Quick question: have we confirmed A100 quota with the cloud team? I recall a soft cap in that region.
Diego: I opened quota ticket #87421 yesterday. Cloud estimated ~48h processing.
Elena: Added a networking validation block — check MTU, subnet sizes, route tables across AZs. Also noted NLB health-check ports and idle-timeouts.
SRE-bot: deploy-notify: new runbook draft uploaded to /docs/region-runbooks/eu-central-2.md by Maya at 2026-03-12T09:14Z
Maya: Checklist (short):
- confirm GPU quota + instance family availability
- create control-plane VMs (secure boot off for driver installs)
- install GPU drivers, CUDA; run nvidia-smi
- bootstrap k8s nodes; add taints/labels for gpu pools
- verify kv-cache mount (NFS) and permissions
- perf smoke test (throughput / p50 latency)
- validate KMS policies and audit logging
Owen: Drivers: pin driver version and validate kernel ABI before production. Last time DKMS caused nodes to boot into mismatched kernels.
Diego: Add iperf3 test between control and GPU nodes — MTU mismatch killed large model downloads for me once.
Elena: For NLBs, prefer instance-target groups (not IP) to avoid target drift when autoscaling. Healthcheck TCP 80/443 recommended.
Maya: Updated doc with kernel ABI checks, iperf3, and a small "Known Issues" troubleshooting table.
Owen: Can you paste the exact smoke-test commands? Example idea: run a pod from nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:23.05 and execute a tiny bench script.
Maya: Added snippet:
```
kubectl apply -f gpu-smoketest.yaml
kubectl logs -f smoketest-pod
# expect >100 tokens/sec on A100-small baseline
```
Elena: Add quick cost sanity: baseline monthly for hot-standby vs burst-only. Cost-Ops can add numbers.
Cost-Ops: Quick calc: 8x A100-80GB committed ≈ €28k/mo in eu-central-2. Spot/burst mix can reduce ~40%.
Owen: Handoff checklist to oncall:
- link runbook
- escalation contacts (infra oncall, cloud rep, vendor)
- rollback: scale down GPU ASG, failover to eu-west-1 fallback
- kernel driver rollback playbook
Maya: Added oncall contact block and rollback steps. Marked eu-west-1 as fallback for low-latency customers.
Diego: Known issue: NVMe requeue spikes during heavy checkpointing — workaround: smaller checkpoints, async flush.
Elena: Also: intermittent EFS permission errors during scale events. Workaround: wait-for-fstab + systemd mount retry.
Maya: Included wait loop:
```
for i in {1..12}; do mountpoint -q /mnt/kv && break || sleep 5; done
if ! mountpoint -q /mnt/kv; then systemctl restart nfs-client.target
fi
```
Owen: Acceptance gate idea: run nightly perf for 3 consecutive runs within 10% of baseline before product handoff.
Maya: Added acceptance gate: 3/3 perf runs within 10% and no failed healthchecks for 1h.
Cost-Ops: I'll attach a cost appendix and sensitivity table (spot% vs committed) to the runbook.
Elena: Add an "escalation hints" section: quick logs to grab — dmesg, kubelet, nvidia-smi -q, /var/log/cloud-init. Include sample collector commands.
Maya: Done. Also left a TODO to add vendor driver compatibility table once vendor confirms versions.
Diego: +1 from infra. Scheduling handoff meeting with oncall tomorrow 09:00 CET.
SRE-bot: reminder: handoff-meeting scheduled by Diego for 2026-03-13T09:00:00+01:00
Maya: Thanks all — will convert to official runbook after quota clears and Cost-Ops attachments land.
